name: Cold waves & winter storms
summary: No top-tier cold or winter-storm warning across a major region on 25 Nov; China's 15–19 Nov cold wave has passed
state: A cold wave brought temperature drops of up to 17°C, blizzards and road closures to northern China from 15 to 19 Nov (The Watchers), following an earlier wave from 8 to 10 Nov that prompted a red blizzard warning in Qinhuangdao (Global Times). US outlooks for Thanksgiving on 26 Nov point to possible snow in the Upper Midwest, Rockies and Great Lakes, but no formal warnings were found (Mental Floss). Searches on 25 Nov found no top-tier warning across a major region and no cold-related power or gas outages, so Normal holds.
for_you: Travellers in the northern US around 26 Nov may meet snow on roads and at airports; check the National Weather Service. In the UK, the Met Office issues any cold or snow warnings.
rubric_hit: Normal: no major cold wave or winter storm affecting large populations found on 25 Nov

why: Severe cold and winter storms kill, cut power and spike gas demand, as in Texas in 2021; they matter most when energy supplies are tight.
drivers: Polar vortex disruption, blocking highs, ENSO, Arctic outbreaks.

rubric.alert: Deadly cold or winter storms with widespread power or gas outages.
rubric.watch: Top-tier cold or winter-storm warnings across a major region, or a cold wave lifting gas demand sharply.
rubric.normal: No major cold wave or winter storm affecting large populations.
